original_question: Let Phi be the associated-form map from nondegenerate homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n to homogeneous degree n(d-2) forms on the dual space. Repeated application of this construction gives iterates such as Phi^2 when defined as rational maps between the corresponding spaces of forms. Is Phi^k a well-defined rational map for every positive integer k?
target_in_paper: The paper-faithful target is the result, reviewed in the section on binary quartics and ternary cubics, that only in the self-dual degree cases (n,d)=(2,4) and (n,d)=(3,3) does the associated-form construction give a rational self-map on projective space, and in those cases the induced map is a rational SL_n-equivariant involution.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the associated-form map Φ, its domain as nondegenerate homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n, and the idea of composing the construction. It also correctly notices that one must interpret repeated application as a rational map between spaces of forms.
missing_details: The paper does not ask about Φ^k for arbitrary k; the nearby official statement is much narrower: the involution phenomenon for the special cases (n,d)=(2,4) and (n,d)=(3,3).
To get a self-map at all, one must require n(d-2)=d; otherwise Φ changes the degree and does not define a rational self-map of the same projective space.
Solving n(d-2)=d with n>=2 and d>=3 gives exactly the two cases treated in the paper: binary quartics and ternary cubics.
The map is considered after projectivization: the paper discusses the induced rational map on P(Q_n^d), not an unrestricted iterate on affine spaces of varying degree.
One must specify the ambient field C and the notation Q_n^d for the vector space of degree-d forms on C^n.
The domain is the discriminant-nonvanishing locus X_n^d={f in Q_n^d : Δ(f)≠0}.
To interpret Φ^2 one must identify (C^n)^{**} with C^n.
The official result is that the induced rational self-map is an involution, i.e. P(Φ)^2=id as a rational map; it is not a question about all higher iterates.
Your draft omits the projective formulation and therefore misses the exact setting in which the paper states the result.
refined_question: Let Q_n^d denote the complex vector space of homogeneous degree-d forms on C^n, let X_n^d={f in Q_n^d: Δ(f)≠0}, and let Φ:X_n^d→Q_n^{n(d-2)*} be the associated-form morphism. In the only cases for which n(d-2)=d, namely (n,d)=(2,4) and (n,d)=(3,3), after identifying (C^n)^{**} with C^n, does Φ descend to a nontrivial rational SL_n-equivariant involution P(Φ):P(Q_n^d)⇢P(Q_n^d), equivalently satisfying P(Φ)^2=id as a rational map?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper's discussion of composing the associated-form construction, but it broadens the issue beyond the paper's actual scope. In the paper, the key point is that one only gets a rational self-map after projectivization and only when the output degree n(d-2) equals the input degree d. This forces the two special cases of binary quartics and ternary cubics. The paper then reviews the theorem that, in exactly these cases, the induced projective map is a rational equivariant involution. So the draft should be sharpened from a question about arbitrary iterates Φ^k to the precise involution statement in the only self-dual degree cases.
